transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess what finally pushed me to come in is my appetite has been really inconsistent for months. Some days I just skip dinner without really meaning to, and I’ve lost some weight without trying. Other nights I’ll just pick at crackers or cereal because cooking just for myself feels… kind of pointless.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?
I’m not really sure I’d call it depressed. I’ve felt kind of low at times, but it’s hard for me to pin down.
Do you live alone?
I’m not sure how that’s relevant, but… I’d rather not get into my living situation right now.
Have you been feeling sad or down most days?
I don’t know if it’s most days. I have days where I feel pretty low, but I haven’t really been keeping track of how often.
Have you been enjoying the things you usually like to do less than before?

Yeah… I think so. I still do things I used to enjoy, like watering the garden or going to book club, but it doesn’t really feel the same. A lot of the time it just feels flat, and I either leave early or don’t get myself started at all.
Have you been avoiding other people more than usual?

Yeah… I have. I’m still going to work, but I’m not keeping up the way I used to. My notes and documentation pile up, and I end up staying late to fix things that used to be easy for me.

Outside of work, I’ve really pulled back. I don’t see friends much, and even basic routines have kind of shrunk down to almost nothing.
Have you had thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of hurting yourself?

I haven’t made any plan to hurt myself. But… yes, sometimes I catch myself thinking it would be a relief if I just didn’t wake up. And that scares me, because I know if a client said that to me, I’d take it seriously.
Did these changes start after something stressful happened in your life?
Yes. It started around when my divorce was finalized. It’s been… about a year and seven months now, and I feel like I haven’t really gotten back to myself since then.
For at least two weeks at a time, have you felt down or unable to enjoy things nearly every day?
Yes. I mean… I still do some of the things I used to enjoy, like watering the garden or going to book club, but it mostly feels flat. A lot of the time I leave early, or I just don’t start at all.
Are you avoiding food because you’re worried about gaining weight or about your body shape?
No, I don’t think so. I’m not avoiding food because of my weight or body shape.
Have you been feeling this way continuously for at least two years?
No, not quite two years. It’s been since the divorce was finalized, so about a year and seven months.
Before this started after your divorce, had you ever gone through another period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed or lost interest in things most days?
I’m not sure. I don’t really remember another stretch like this before the divorce, at least not clearly.
Have you been feeling worthless or blaming yourself a lot?

Yes. I do blame myself a lot. I keep going back over the marriage in my head and thinking I must have failed at something basic. Part of me knows it’s not that simple, but I still end up feeling that way.
Have you been moving or speaking noticeably slower than usual?
I haven’t really noticed that, no. I mean, I feel slower getting through the day sometimes, but I don’t think I’m actually moving or talking slower in a way other people would notice.
Have you ever had a period when you felt unusually energized or high compared with your normal self?
I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve had normal good moods or busy days, but not a period where I felt unusually high or energized compared to myself.
